newsitem.title: USA: Sears May same-store sales off, weather cited.
newsitem.headline: Sears May same-store sales off, weather cited.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co said domestic same-store revenues for the four weeks ended May 31 declined 1.2 percent, compared with a 10.2 percent increase in the same period a year ago.
Total domestic store revenues for the month were $2.14 billion, 4.2 percent above revenues of $2.05 billion for the four weeks ending June 1, 1996, Sears said.

"Unseasonably cool weather in much of the country delayed the sales of air conditioners, riding mowers and tractors, and other seasonal product lines which affected overall domestic store results," said chief executive Arthur Martinez.

"May was a month marked by sharp contrasts," Martinez said. "Sears full-line stores continued to generate solid growth in softlines, while hardlines sales were down. Women's ready to wear, footwear, fine jewelry, and cosmetics and fragrances posted double-digit sales increases."
He added, "In regions not affected by cool weather, such as the Northwest and Southwest, overall sales were strong."
For the 17 weeks ending May 31, Sears reported total revenues of $11.85 billion, 6.1 percent above the $11.17 billion in the prior-year period.
